name: Venkatraman Viswanathan
current_role: Founder & Chairperson, Latent View Analytics (Chennai / San Jose)
profile: IIT Madras civil engineer and IIM Calcutta MBA who co-founded data-analytics firm LatentView in 2006 with his wife Pramad Jandhyala; CEO 2006-2014, then chairperson with professional CEOs. LatentView's Nov 2021 IPO raised Rs 600 crore and was subscribed 338x. In 2026 the board named ex-Wipro executive Sonal Ramrakhiani CEO (effective July 15, 2026).
interesting_fact: LatentView's November 2021 IPO was oversubscribed 338 times and listed at roughly a 160% premium to its issue price, a record subscription level for an Indian IPO at the time.
deep_cut_fact: An old LatentView corporate bio says that outside analytics he 'indulges his passion for technological gadgets' (then a Squeezebox wireless radio streaming music and news from around the world) and is a value investor in public markets. He received IIM Calcutta's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2024.
notes: Goes by 'Venkat'. venkat@latentview.com is embedded in the board-of-directors listing on LatentView's corporate information page. He's a strong fit for a data/AI episode and writes for Forbes Technology Council and Entrepreneur.

name: Ke Yunfeng
current_role: Chairman, DaShenLin Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603233)
profile: Guangdong-born founder and chairman of DaShenLin, one of China's largest pharmacy chains. It opened its first store in 1999, listed in Shanghai in 2017, and now runs thousands of outlets with more than 23,000 employees. He controls the company with relatives Ke Jinlong and Ke Kangbao under a 2015 concert-party agreement and holds about 21% himself.
interesting_fact: DaShenLin opened its first store in 1999 and has grown to more than 4,000 pharmacies with over 23,000 employees.
deep_cut_fact: As a deputy to China's National People's Congress, he proposed at the 2020 'Two Sessions' that retail pharmacies be formally brought into the public-health emergency system, drawing on pharmacies' role during COVID-19.
notes: The IR email belongs to the board secretary (Peng Guangzhi) and is published in DaShenLin's periodic reports. Outreach would need to be in Chinese. Birth year (1967) and early career (Maoming audit bureau) come only from aggregator sites and are unverified.

name: Wu Xidun
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Tonze New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (formerly Guangdong Tonze Electric; SZSE: 002759)
profile: Shantou-based entrepreneur (Chinese national, Hong Kong resident, CEIBS EMBA) who built Tonze, a small-kitchen-appliance maker founded in 1996 and known for electric stew pots. Via its subsidiary Jiangsu Xintai Materials, Tonze moved into lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6), an electrolyte salt for EV batteries, and renamed itself Tonze New Energy Technology.
interesting_fact: His company pivoted from slow cookers and health kettles to supplying LiPF6, a key lithium-ion battery electrolyte material, and now describes its focus as 'clean energy and healthy appliances'.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Tonze he is executive director of Chaozhou Tonze Ceramics Industrial Co. and of a Shantou testing-technology company, and he holds an EMBA from CEIBS (China Europe International Business School).
notes: zwl@tonze.com is the board secretary's (Zheng Wenlong) email, from the 2025 annual report. The 2025 report also mentions a pending CSRC investigation notice, so check its status before outreach. The battery-materials angle fits an energy episode. The deep-cut source is a brand-aggregator profile; the Chaozhou Tonze Ceramics directorship is from that profile.

name: William Morrison
current_role: Private investor; Morrisons supermarket heir (no public executive role found)
profile: Most likely the son of the late Sir Ken Morrison (1931-2017), who built Bradford-based Wm Morrison Supermarkets. The business was founded by his grandfather William Murdoch Morrison (1878-1956). The heir (about 43 in 2019) shares the family fortune, put at roughly £900m+ by the Sunday Times Rich List, with his siblings, and keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: The business that became Morrisons was started in 1899 by William Murdoch Morrison selling eggs and butter wholesale from a stall in Bradford. In 2015 the heir William and his father Sir Ken together held about 4.7 million shares in rival Sainsbury's.
notes: The name is ambiguous. The founder William Murdoch Morrison died in 1956 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morrison_(businessman)), so this listing is most likely Sir Ken's son William, who has no public role, website or published contact. Morrisons itself was taken private by CD&R in 2021. Not a strong podcast prospect.

name: Sun Weiwen
current_role: Director / Vice Chairman, Guangdong Taienkang (T&K) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (SZSE ChiNext: 301263)
profile: Co-founder and major shareholder of Shantou-based Guangdong Taienkang Pharmaceutical (T&K), founded in 1999, which acts as agent-operator for pharma brands and develops, makes and sells drugs and medical devices. She co-controls the company with her husband, chairman Zheng Hanjie. She previously founded Guangdong Quanyoujia Family Service Technology in 2002.
interesting_fact: She holds MBAs from three institutions: South China University of Technology, Macau University of Science & Technology, and Lingnan College at Sun Yat-sen University.
notes: Ms. Sun; T&K = Taienkang (泰恩康). The IR email belongs to the board secretary's office (Li Ting), per the 2025 annual report summary. MarketScreener puts her stake value at about $226M (Oct 2026), well under billionaire level now. Outreach would need to be in Chinese.

name: Chan Wing Hong
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, Plover Bay Technologies (HKEX: 1523); Founder & CEO of Peplink
profile: Hong Kong engineer-entrepreneur (Alex Chan) who founded Peplink in 2006 to build bonded multi-WAN and cellular routers (SpeedFusion), later adding the Pepwave wireless line. He took the parent, Plover Bay, public in Hong Kong. In Feb 2026 Plover Bay announced a plan to spin off Peplink Holdings as a separate Nasdaq listing, expected to close by the end of 2026.
interesting_fact: Peplink filed its first US patent on WAN-bonding in 2009. The technology became SpeedFusion, now used to bond cellular and Starlink links for vehicles, ships and public-safety fleets.
deep_cut_fact: In a post on Peplink's own community forum he summed up the company plainly: 'Fundamentally, we are in the modem business.' He noted that its ~200 staff span Taiwan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Hong Kong, Lithuania, the UK and Canada, and that the founding team is still with the company.
notes: Known publicly as Alex Chan. He posts directly on forum.peplink.com, which could be a low-key route. The pending Peplink Nasdaq spinoff is a timely hook, and the connectivity/Starlink angle fits a data-center or infra episode. No published IR email found; the HKEX filings list the company secretary.

name: Zhou Quan
profile: One of the earliest members of IDG's China venture team (joined 1993). Alongside founding chairman Xiong Xiaoge, he is one of the two best-known investors at IDG Capital, which backed waves of Chinese internet companies. Through IDG-affiliated funds he appears in SEC filings as a 10% owner of stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL), whose round IDG led back in Circle's early China push.
interesting_fact: IDG Capital led a $60 million round in Circle, the US fintech behind the USDC stablecoin, to back its China expansion; Zhou is now listed in SEC insider filings as a ten-percent owner of the public Circle Internet Group.
deep_cut_fact: When IDG partners Zhang Zhen, Gao Xiang and Yue Bin left to start Gaorong Capital, Zhou helped rewrite their business plan, personally introduced Accel partners as LPs and invested as an LP himself. Gaorong closed a first fund of over $200M within three months.
notes: Very low public profile. In 2018 he and Xiong Xiaoge said they would stop taking part in investor rankings 'to leave the opportunity to young people'. The best route is IDG Capital's media email. The Circle/stablecoin and Chinese-VC angles are the hooks.

name: Nazar M. Khan
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Technology Officer & Board Member, TeraWulf Inc. (Nasdaq: WULF)
profile: Energy-infrastructure dealmaker who co-founded TeraWulf, which began as a zero-carbon bitcoin miner at Lake Mariner, NY and has repositioned as a power-first AI/HPC data-center developer. The company says it now controls about 2.3 GW of power capacity. As CTO he oversees hardware procurement, site evaluation and infrastructure buildout; he spent nearly 20 years as EVP of Beowulf Energy LLC before that.
interesting_fact: TeraWulf now pitches itself as 'energy operators first', arguing that in AI compute 'energy expertise is the moat', and says it controls about 2.3 gigawatts of power across sites such as Lake Mariner (NY).
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto and AI he spent nearly two decades as EVP at Beowulf Energy, leading its power-plant acquisitions and development; earlier he worked in investment banking and private equity at Evercore. He holds both a B.S. and a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania.
notes: A strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. TeraWulf's 'Reach Out' page and Media section at terawulf.com/news are the official routes. No dedicated IR/press email was found on the IR contacts page. Not a classic billionaire; he is in this list as an SEC insider.

name: Irving Tan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Western Digital Corporation (Nasdaq: WDC); Chairman, SATS Ltd.
profile: Singaporean executive who became CEO of Western Digital when it separated from its flash business (SanDisk) in Feb 2025, leaving a pure-play hard-drive maker serving AI/cloud data centers. Before that he was WD's EVP of Global Operations (manufacturing, supply chain, IT) and spent years at Cisco, rising to EVP & Global Chief of Operations and Chairperson for Asia Pacific, Japan & China.
interesting_fact: He runs a US data-storage giant while also chairing the board of SATS (Singapore Airport Terminal Services) and sitting on the board of the U.S.-Japan Business Council.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer: both his bachelor's in mechanical engineering and his MBA are from Singapore's Nanyang Technological University, which also gave him an honorary doctorate. He has advised governments on using technology to transform.
notes: Hired-CEO insider, not a founder. The AI-driven demand for high-capacity HDDs in data centers is the podcast hook. Route via WD corporate communications. The Feb 2025 timing comes from WD's own 'The Future of HDDs Begins Now' post (Feb 22, 2025).

name: Zhang Wendong
current_role: Founder and chairman, Edifier Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002351)
profile: Beijing entrepreneur who founded audio maker Edifier in May 1996. Edifier went public in 2010, the first listed audio-speaker company in China, and now sells speakers and headphones in 70+ countries. Under his leadership Edifier bought Japanese electrostatic-headphone maker STAX (2011), invested in US planar-headphone maker Audeze (2016), and marked its 30th anniversary in 2026.
interesting_fact: Edifier acquired STAX, the storied Japanese maker of electrostatic 'earspeakers', in 2011, giving a Chinese speaker brand a foothold in the high-end audiophile market.
deep_cut_fact: Edifier's Airpulse hi-fi speaker brand was developed with veteran audio engineer Phil Jones, and its 2013 gaming sub-brand is called Hecate.
notes: Wikipedia gives the name as 'Wen Dong Zhang'. Role verification is thin because search quota ran out mid-lane; check his current title and the company's IR email in Edifier's latest SZSE annual report. Outreach would likely need to be in Chinese.

name: Chung King Yee
current_role: Shareholder in Truly International Holdings (HKEX: 0732); spouse of founder-chairman Lam Wai Wah (no executive role disclosed)
profile: Chung King Yee, Cecilia, is the wife of Lam Wai Wah, who founded and chairs Hong Kong-listed Truly International, a maker of LCD/AMOLED displays, touch panels and camera modules for phones and cars. Truly's 2025 annual report shows her holding 74.8 million Truly shares beneficially; her husband is deemed interested in them. She is not listed as a director or executive.
interesting_fact: Truly's Huizhou 4.5-generation AMOLED production line entered mass production in 2016, and its fifth-generation TFT-LCD line lit up its first product in 2018. Founder Lam Wai Wah has more than 40 years in electronics.
notes: A passive shareholder with no public profile. The wealth listing probably reflects the Lam/Chung family's Truly stake. The annual report says enquiry@truly.com.hk is the route for questions to the board and senior management; outreach is better aimed at chairman Lam Wai Wah. Alive status not confirmed independently, though she is listed as holding shares as of 31 Dec 2025.

name: Chen Zhuonan
current_role: Member of the Chen founding family of Agile Group Holdings (HKEX: 3383); current personal title not verified
profile: Listed under Agile, the Zhongshan-born property developer founded in 1992 by the Chen family and led by chairman and president Chen Zhuo Lin. notes: Web-search quota ran out before Chen Zhuonan's own bio could be checked, so his exact relationship (likely a brother of Chen Zhuo Lin) and role are unverified; check Agile's annual-report director section on HKEXnews. The real-estate profile doesn't fit an energy/data-center podcast well.
